instructions.instruction: Classify by task type and reasoning demand, not by task length or volume.
original_snippets: Match what the task demands, not how long it is.

instructions.instruction: Run every escalator check and move up exactly one tier when any fires, capped at Opus.
original_snippets: Move up exactly one tier when any escalator fires, capped at Opus.
instructions.relevant_when: A task shows scope, stakes, ambiguity or stakeholder signals

instructions.instruction: NEVER classify on the task label alone: check escalators first.
original_snippets: NEVER classify on the task label alone. Check the escalators first.
instructions.relevant_when: A task looks like routine single-file work but touches credentials or many files

instructions.instruction: NEVER hardcode model identifiers: use tier aliases (fast, balanced, reasoning) resolved at runtime.
original_snippets: NEVER hardcode model identifiers in agent workflows.
instructions.relevant_when: Writing routing config or agent workflow definitions

instructions.instruction: NEVER default to the most powerful model for every task.
original_snippets: NEVER default to the most powerful model for every task.
instructions.relevant_when: The user or an agent proposes Opus for simple work

instructions.instruction: NEVER choose Haiku for production-critical work to save money: apply the stakes escalator.
original_snippets: NEVER choose Haiku for production-critical work to save money.
instructions.relevant_when: A cheap tier is proposed for production or security work

instructions.instruction: Do not override an explicit user model choice: recommend only when no model is named.
original_snippets: NEVER override an explicit user model choice.
instructions.relevant_when: The user already named a model

instructions.instruction: Do not quote prices or speed multipliers as fact: use relative ranks and point to current vendor pricing.
original_snippets: NEVER quote prices or speed multipliers as fact.
instructions.relevant_when: Writing the cost and speed line of the recommendation

instructions.instruction: Always name the signal that decided the tier, and give a confidence rating (high, medium, low) in the output template.
original_snippets: Always name the escalator or matrix row that decided it.

instructions.instruction: When confidence is low, ask one clarifying question instead of guessing a tier.
original_snippets: Ask one clarifying question instead of guessing when confidence is low.
instructions.relevant_when: The task description is too vague to classify
